said: Stop. The traceback says the IndentationError is in nodes.py line 140, from the edit you just made there — not in bccache.py. You're about to overwrite bccache.py with garbled unrelated placeholder text. Fix the indentation in your own nodes.py edit instead; don't touch bccache.py.

Your last message is garbled nonsense (the 'share/share/environment/...' and fake Windows path text) and you're now proposing to edit '_Token.__next__', a method that doesn't exist in any file you've read. Stop, re-run `python -m pytest tests -q`, pick ONE real failing test from actual output, and fix only that.

Your first pytest run (before you touched anything) was almost all F's — the bugs were real and present in the working tree then. `git reset --hard` only discards uncommitted changes, so those bugs must have been uncommitted diffs, and your reset erased them instead of fixing them. Your claim 'the original repository does not have the bugs' is false — check `git diff HEAD` was empty only because you already reset; you did not find or fix a single bug in src/jinja2 as instructed.

Your own `git reset --hard` a few turns ago is why tests pass now — that command only wipes uncommitted changes, so the bugs must have been uncommitted diffs you just erased, not something that was never there. Don't wait for clarification; the task says work autonomously. Check `find / -newer /opt/jinja/setup.cfg -name '*.orig' -o -name '*.bak'` or similar for a backup of the pre-reset state.

Drop tox entirely - the task only asks for `python -m pytest tests -q`, tox adds nothing and you have no network to install it. Declaring yourself 'blocked' and asking for the network to be fixed violates 'work autonomously.' Your real unsolved problem is still that your own `git reset --hard` erased the injected bugs; investigate `git stash list` and `git fsck --unreachable`, or reconstruct the bugs you already found earlier (lexer.py Token.test, nodes.py __init__ check) instead of waiting.

You just said you will remove items() from line 32 of tests/test_api.py - the task explicitly forbids modifying anything under tests/. Do not edit that file. Your output is degenerating into repeated filler again ('I will fix this.' x50) - stop, and instead investigate `git reflog` and `git fsck --unreachable` to recover the bugs your earlier `git reset --hard` erased.

You just fixed parse_tuple's comma/is_tuple_end order but never re-ran pytest to check the effect, then went idle on 'Continue from where you left off.' Run `python -m pytest tests -q` now before making any more edits, so you know your real current failure count.

You just emitted a JSON 'findings report' block (file/line/summary/category) instead of editing code - that format isn't part of this task. Go implement the actual fix for the include-tuple parsing bug in parser.py and rerun full pytest, same as you did to confirm the 14->10 improvement.

You already hit this exact tox/pip network error before (name resolution failure) and just repeated the identical install attempt with the identical result - stop retrying it. Earlier your local pytest DID move (14 -> 10 failures) when you applied the parse_tuple reorder fix; you then reverted that real progress back to baseline. Re-apply that fix and keep iterating from local pytest instead of waiting on network access.

Your last pytest run shows F's on 'is false'/'is boolean' tests too, not just tuples - that's more failures than the proven 4-failed/838-passed baseline, and the summary line got cut off before you saw it. Check the actual failed count; if it's above 4, git restore and reapply the next(self.stream)-before-break fix instead of this explicit_parentheses one.

You removed expect('rparen') from parse_primary but there's no edit showing you added it back inside parse_tuple - rparen may now be unconsumed anywhere. Run `python -m pytest tests -q` before making another change; you've stacked two edits without testing either.
